_meta.topic: Land purchase due diligence, construction finance, warranties and insurance, construction delays, building control and permit charges, and what appliances add to value or rent

conventions.sourceType: 'primary' when the page belongs to the authority, insurer, lender or company whose figure it is; otherwise 'secondary'
conventions.confirmed: true when the figure was read directly from the cited page or document during this session; false when it came only from a search-engine excerpt or a page that could not be opened, or when it is a broad market estimate
conventions.nulls: null with a note where no published figure was found; nothing here is invented
conventions.arithmetic: Where a premium is given for a sample amount, it was computed by this researcher from the published rate table. The computation is shown in the note.

_meta.correctionToBrief: The brief described TIRSA zone 1 as NYC. It is the other way round: every New York City county (Bronx, Kings, New York, Queens, Richmond) is in zone 2, along with Long Island, Westchester, the Hudson Valley and Albany. Zone 1 is western, central and northern upstate (Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse, the North Country and so on). Zone 2 rates include the title search. Zone 1 rates do not, and the search is billed separately.

source.publisher: Title Insurance Rate Service Association (TIRSA), approved by the NY Department of Financial Services

titleInsurance.note: Read from the rate manual text, Rule on rate zones. The tirsa.org link refused connections during this session; the identical manual hosted by Fidelity National Financial's rate calculator was read instead. Individual insurers may file deviations (for example WFG files a lower deviation), so a quoted premium can differ from the TIRSA base.

titleInsurance.item: Owner's policy premium, TIRSA base rates
titleInsurance.note: Rates read from Part II of the manual. Examples computed here: zone 1 at $100,000 = 338 + 15 x 7.52 + 50 x 4.69; at $250,000 add 150 x 3.78; at $500,000 add 400 x 3.78 to the $100,000 figure. Zone 2 is the same method with its own rates. Loan-policy per-$1,000 rates follow the same eight brackets in order. These are premiums only: endorsements, the zone 1 search charge, recording and closing fees are extra.

titleInsurance.item: Owner's policy premium, Old Republic Title partial rate schedule for Los Angeles
titleInsurance.note: California rates are filed by each underwriter rather than promulgated, so First American and Fidelity charge different amounts. The homeowner's policy is 110% of the standard owner's rate here. Escrow fees are separate and not included.

titleInsurance.item: Owner's policy premium, CATIC standard and expanded protection
titleInsurance.note: Read from CATIC's published schedule. It is the most recent CATIC schedule found online and is dated 2016, so a newer filing may exist; treat it as the last published CATIC rate rather than a confirmed current one. Expanded (homeowner's) policy is about 110% of standard.

titleInsurance.item: Owner's policy premium, WFG National Title filed rate manual (cross-check on CATIC)
titleInsurance.note: Examples computed here and rounded per the manual's rule (49 cents or less dropped): $100,000 = 109 + 80 x 4.36; $250,000 adds 100 x 4.09 and 50 x 3.54; $500,000 adds 100 x 4.09 and 300 x 3.54 to the $100,000 figure.

Canadian insurers (FCT, Stewart, Chicago Title, TitlePLUS) do not publish residential rate tables; premiums are quoted through the lawyer or notary and are usually flat. Figure from a search excerpt only. Treat as a modeled estimate.

survey.note: From search excerpt. HomeAdvisor's 2025 page gives a much lower average ($546), which likely reflects small residential lot surveys; the two are not reconciled. Angi also publishes city pages for Los Angeles and New York (https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-land-survey-cost/ny/new-york) that were not opened.

phaseIEnvironmental.item: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment to ASTM E1527-21

value.riskyPriorUseAdjustment: gas stations and dry cleaners add 30-60%

phaseIEnvironmental.note: Search excerpt. A Phase I is standard for commercial land and lenders; it is rarely ordered for an ordinary residential lot. No official fee exists; these are consultant market prices.

legalFees.item: Real estate attorney flat fee for a residential purchase
legalFees.note: Search excerpts from several firm pages; no official schedule exists. New York practice is a flat fee per closing, with an attorney for each side.

source.publisher: HomeOwners Alliance, citing reallymoving Conveyancing Costs Index Q2 2026

legalFees.note: Based on about 34,000 quotes. No London-only figure was published on the page; London quotes typically run higher. Excludes Stamp Duty Land Tax. A leasehold purchase usually costs around £300 more.

legalFees.item: Solicitor's fee for a residential purchase
legalFees.note: Search excerpts. Fees are quoted plus 23% VAT and outlays. The 1% model is still seen but flat fees are now more common in Dublin and Kildare.

legalFees.item: Real estate lawyer fee for a purchase
legalFees.note: Search excerpts. Plus 13% HST and disbursements.

legalFees.item: Lawyer or notary fee for a purchase
legalFees.note: Search excerpts. In BC a notary public can handle conveyancing, and fees are comparable to a lawyer's.

subdivision.item: Preliminary parcel map filing fee, up to 4 lots

source.publisher: City of Los Angeles, Municipal Code Sec. 19.02 (via American Legal Publishing)
source.date: CPI-adjusted annually each July 1; 3.50% adjustment effective 2024-07-01

subdivision.note: Figures from a search excerpt of the municipal code; the code page and the Planning Department's CPI schedule (https://planning.lacity.gov/odocument/ca4fb8e8-1bb8-4f52-8203-4f93fcff93c8/2024_annual_fee_adjustment.pdf) both refused access. Surcharges and later CPI adjustments are not included.

subdivision.place: New York (Town of Rochester, Ulster County; TIRSA zone 2)
subdivision.note: Escrow pays the town's consultants and is drawn down, then refunded or topped up.

value.smithtown_SuffolkCounty_residential: 2000 plus 1100 per lot or dwelling unit (April 2025)
value.clinton_DutchessCounty_minor: 500 plus 300 per lot and 300 per dwelling (2025)

subdivision.note: Search excerpts from each town's own fee schedule (Clinton: https://www.clintondcny.gov/wp-content/uploads/RES-10-OF-2025-THE-FEE-SCHEDULE-2.11.25-2.pdf; Yorktown: https://www.yorktownny.gov/media/454no14b/feeschedule-minorsub.pdf; Newburgh: https://www.townofnewburghny.gov/FCpdf/FEE%20SCHEDULE%20TOTAL%20PACKAGE.doc). Not opened. No zone 1 (western or central upstate) town schedule was gathered.

constructionFinance.place: United States (Florida credit union; example of a published rate sheet)
constructionFinance.note: Florida lender, not NY, CT or CA; no lender in those three states was found publishing construction rates online (Mid-Hudson Valley FCU and Hudson Valley CU describe the product without rates).

constructionFinance.place: United States (Hawaii credit union; example of a published rate sheet)
constructionFinance.note: Matches the 12-month, interest-only, 20% down pattern in the brief. The $1,000 deposit covers appraisal, credit report, inspection and flood certification.
Search excerpt; market summary, not a lender's rate.
Funds are released in arrears as the build adds value, not at fixed milestones. Interest-only during the build needs a repayment vehicle.

value.epcDiscount: 0.50 to 1.50 points off for EPC B or better

constructionFinance.note: Ecology suggests a 35% deposit on the plot plus funds for the early build stages.

constructionFinance.item: BuildStore Accelerator self-build mortgage (stage payments in advance)

value.stageTiming: released at the start of each stage

constructionFinance.note: LTV and in-advance timing read from the page. The rate range came from a search excerpt of a BuildStore page and was not shown on the page opened; BuildStore is a broker, so the range spans several lenders.

constructionFinance.item: Bank of Ireland self-build mortgage (stage payments)
constructionFinance.note: Each stage is certified by the borrower's own architect or engineer. The rate is the bank's standard variable or fixed mortgage rate; no separate self-build rate is published. Other Irish lenders: AIB 4 to 6 stages; PTSB up to 6.

warrantyInsurance.item: Builder's 1-2-10 structural warranty (2-10 Home Buyers Warranty)
warrantyInsurance.note: The under-0.5% figure was read on the page; the $500 to $1,000 range is from a 2-10 blog excerpt and was not opened. Bought by the builder, usually; an owner-builder normally cannot enroll.

The average is across Insureon's small-business customers, not specifically single-family homes. Other sources quote as little as 0.1% to 0.55% of completed value; the published ranges disagree by an order of magnitude, so treat the 1-4% as the upper, broker-quoted band.
Dated 2020. Providers named for self-build: LABC Warranty, Self Build Zone, BuildCare, Protek, ProAktive. The surcharge is the extra premium when cover is bought after work has started.
Terms from search excerpts of LABC Warranty pages. LABC gives a price only through its online indication form; no published price.

NHBC publishes no price; the premium depends on the registered builder's rating and the sale price. Its custom-build page does not describe a self-build product, and Premier Guarantee also appears not to cover self-builders. A £1,500 to £3,500 figure circulates on secondary sites but was not traced to NHBC.
HomeBond says it is a fixed price per dwelling but does not publish the price. The €2,500 to €5,000 estimate is from planningpermissionireland.ie (secondary, unconfirmed).

warrantyInsurance.item: Tarion new home enrolment fee (paid by the builder or vendor, usually passed to the buyer)
warrantyInsurance.note: Fees before 13% HST. A search excerpt quoted older fees (for example $970 for $500,000 to $550,000); the page read here supersedes it. The 7-year term and $400,000 limit are from a search excerpt.
From search excerpts of BC Housing pages. A licensed builder in BC must instead buy 2-5-10 home warranty insurance; no published premium was found.

delays.item: Average months from start to completion, new single-family houses, by purpose of construction

source.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD, Survey of Construction

delays.note: Read from the Census workbook. 'Contractor-built' means built on the owner's land by a general contractor; 'owner-built' means the owner acts as the general contractor. New York and Connecticut fall in the Northeast; California in the West. The relative standard error for US owner-built is 5%. The 1.4-month authorization-to-start figure is from NAHB's Eye on Housing (https://eyeonhousing.org/2026/09/single-family-home-construction-time-declines-in-2025/, Na Zhao, 2026-09-08), which also gives permit-to-completion totals (owner-built 14.3 months, contractor-built 11.7).

delays.item: NAHB Cost of Constructing a Home, 2024

source.publisher: National Association of Home Builders (Eric Lynch)

delays.note: A builder survey of homes built for sale. It does not measure delays or overruns. Its shares of construction cost for the fee lines, as printed: permit fees about 1.8%, impact fee 1.5%, water and sewer 1.5%.

source.publisher: Home Builders Institute study (June 2025), as reported

delays.note: Search excerpt; the HBI study itself was not opened.

delays.item: Renovation budget overrun, Houzz & Home Study
delays.note: Renovations, not new houses. The average size of the overrun is not given on this page.

delays.item: Self-build contingency and budget outcome, NaCSBA Custom and Self Build Market Report 2022

value.outcome: most builds came in on budget or within the contingency

delays.note: The report itself is paywalled (£298). An exact share over budget was not published in the coverage read. A search excerpt claimed about 15% of self-builders went over budget, mostly from upgrading the specification; not traced.

delays.item: Self-build spend, Homebuilding & Renovating market report
delays.note: Survey of about 500 self-builders. No overrun or duration figures.

buildingControl.item: Building control charges, single-storey extension, full plans
buildingControl.note: Figures from a search excerpt of Camden's own schedule; the file returned 403 when opened. Each council in England sets its own charges; a private approved inspector is the alternative.

source.publisher: Irish local authorities (Fingal, Meath, Limerick, Cork County)

buildingControl.note: Search excerpts from council pages; Dublin City's and Kildare's pages did not state the fee. A single house (or an extension over 45 m2) may opt out of statutory certification. Not a plan-review charge like England's.

buildingControl.item: DOB work permit fees, 1-3 family dwellings

source.date: as amended by Local Law 128 of 2024

buildingControl.note: From search excerpts of the code; the code library and ICC copy returned 403. An addition to a house is an alteration permit, so the cost is roughly $130 plus $2.60 per $1,000 of cost above $5,000, before plan-review and other fees.

buildingControl.item: LADBS building permit fee (Table 1-A) and plan check
buildingControl.note: Search excerpt. The base table is CPI-indexed each July 1 and surcharges, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, school fees and sewer charges are added, so real totals for an addition run several thousand dollars. One source says plan check is 85%, another 90%.

buildingControl.item: Building permit fee, one- and two-family residential

value.impliedFormula: 50.26 for the first 1,000, then 27.26 per additional 1,000 (which includes the state's 0.26 per 1,000 education fee)

buildingControl.note: The dollar examples came from a search excerpt; the city page returned 403. The per-$1,000 formula is inferred here from the three examples, which fit it exactly, and is not a published statement.

value.formula: fee = service index x floor area in m2

buildingControl.note: Group C residential (single, semi, town, duplex). A 40 m2 addition would be 742.40.

buildingControl.item: Building permit fee, one-family dwelling addition or alteration
buildingControl.note: Search excerpt; the PDF returned 403. Development permit fees and development cost levies are separate.

value.rule: Appliances not permanently attached are commonly personal property and given no contributory value; built-in appliances can be real property; the appraiser decides, and analyzes missing appliances that are standard in the market for their effect on value or marketability.

source.publisher: Fannie Mae, Appraisal and Property-Related FAQs (Q35)

applianceValue.note: So a freestanding fridge, washer or dryer adds nothing to appraised value, while a built-in range, dishwasher or wall oven can. In a sale contract, freestanding appliances pass only if listed.

applianceValue.item: Rent premium for an in-unit washer-dryer

value.example: a $3,000 apartment rents for about $360 more a month

source.publisher: Gothamist (David Brand), reporting a StreetEasy analysis

applianceValue.note: StreetEasy compared apartments in the same neighborhood with similar size and bedroom count. It is an association, not proof the machine causes the rent difference.

applianceValue.item: Sale premium for an in-unit washer-dryer, condos and co-ops under $2.5M
applianceValue.note: Search excerpt; the page returned 403, so its date and method were not seen.

applianceValue.item: Sale premium for listing keywords (Zillow Home Features That Sell, 2018)
applianceValue.note: About 3.6 million sales from 2016-2017, regression controlling for size, age, location and timing. The premium is over the expected price for homes whose listing uses the phrase, which mostly tags luxury homes, so it overstates what installing the appliance would add. A 3.2% premium for 'new appliances' circulates but was not found in this release.

applianceValue.item: National rent premium for in-unit laundry or a dishwasher
applianceValue.note: No published national rent premium was found. Zillow reports rental listings mentioning in-unit laundry get 76% more saves and 67% more shares per day, which is demand, not a price (search excerpt, unconfirmed).

uncertain: CATIC's Connecticut schedule found is dated 2016-01-01; a later filing may exist. WFG's 2021 CT manual is given as a cross-check.
No title insurance rate table is published for Ontario or British Columbia; the CAD 300-1,000 range is a secondary estimate.
The TIRSA manual used is the Seventh Revision effective 2024-10-01. Individual underwriters can file deviations, so a quoted premium may be lower.
No construction lender in New York, Connecticut or California was found publishing a construction-loan rate; the two published rate sheets used are from Florida and Hawaii credit unions.

LA parcel map fee ($13,204), NYC DOB fee items, Camden building control charges, Vancouver permit fees, New Haven permit examples, the Irish BCMS fees and BC Housing's owner-builder fee all came from search excerpts because the official pages refused automated access (403). The figures are quoted from the official documents' own text, but they were not opened here.
The New Haven formula (first $1,000 at $50.26, then $27.26 per $1,000) is inferred from three examples, not stated.
The NHBC Buildmark premium, LABC self-build price, the HomeBond premium and 2-5-10 warranty premiums in BC are not published.
Builder's risk premium estimates disagree: 1-4% of completed value (brokers) versus 0.1-0.55% (other sources).
No UK statistic was found for the share of self-builds that overrun or by how many months. NaCSBA gives only a 15% average contingency, and its full report is paywalled.
Survey, Phase I, and the attorney, solicitor and conveyancer fees are market estimates from vendors and law-firm pages, not official schedules.
No zone 1 (western or central upstate New York) town subdivision fee schedule was gathered; the Town of Rochester example is in Ulster County (zone 2).
